title: Recipe blog demo: choose the look
question: The roll picked Sunday Food Page. Keep it, take another card, or re-roll.

options.label: Sunday Food Page
options.lineage: the food page of a Pakistani Sunday newspaper magazine: column rules, bilingual headings, a recipe you clip and keep
options.thesis: The blog as this week's food page: today's recipe sits above the fold, every recipe is a clipping you can cut out and keep.
options.viewport: A masthead with the date, today's dish across three columns above a printed fold line, its time, servings and a Clip and keep button, the photo in full colour.
options.risk: Newsprint can feel dull and old if the food photos are small or the grey takes over.

raised.raise: A folded flag marks the step you stopped at, and it is still there when you come back.
A done step is crossed out with a pen mark, not just turned another colour.
Every dish photo is set at the same crop and scale, so the index reads as one set.
Each category keeps one colour band everywhere: rice, karahi, sweets, chai time.
Recipes can be browsed by time of day: sehri, lunch, chai time, dinner.
The fold line is real: what matters most sits above it.

options.label: Ammi’s Notebook
options.lineage: a mother's handwritten recipe copy: ruled pages, ballpoint notes in English and Urdu, a turmeric stain
options.thesis: Every recipe as a page from the family notebook, with the notes your mother would add in the margin.
options.viewport: A ruled notebook page with the dish name in blue ballpoint, the ingredients down the red margin, and the photo pasted in.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for a home cooking blog; it can look like a scrapbook template.

options.label: Select Rail
options.lineage: a film editor's cutting bench: frames on a perforated rail, a tape flag where the editor stopped
options.thesis: Cooking steps as frames on one rail, crossed off as you go, with a flag where you stopped.
options.viewport: A rail of step frames across a dark orange field, the current step open in a white window.
options.case: Holds product clarity (it is a great way to follow steps), but a film bench means nothing to a home cook.
options.risk: Dark and technical in a kitchen.

options.label: Jackfield
options.lineage: a studio patch bay schedule on black glass
options.thesis: Recipes as numbered lanes with amber link lines.
options.viewport: Numbered amber lanes with a recipe in each.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a machine room is the opposite of a kitchen.
options.kept: State shown by a mark, not a colour.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Dishes as fixed-scale plates in a folio.
options.viewport: A row of dish plates at one scale.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too formal and slow for weeknight cooking.

options.label: Colour Bars
options.lineage: a loud modular identity of colour blocks over photos
options.thesis: Categories as big saturated bars over food photos.
options.viewport: Colour bars stacked over a dish photo.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the bars fight the food colours.

options.label: Dawn Cyclorama
options.lineage: a theatre backdrop lit from night to day
options.thesis: Recipes along the day, from sehri dark to dinner.
options.viewport: Bands of light from night to day with meals in each.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dramatic light hides the food.

options.label: Curved Crease
options.lineage: paper folded along one curved crease
options.thesis: The page laid out along one sweeping fold.
options.viewport: One curved fold dividing the page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: elegant, but nothing to do with food.
options.kept: One fold line that organizes the page.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean white food blog with big photos, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: A grid of large dish photos with titles and cooking times, a search bar on top.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other food blog.
